about: The one list of what SecuRAX can do, in plain words. The Command Center, the product website, the docs home page, the README and `./securax features` are all generated from this file by tools/features_sync.py; CI fails if any of them is out of date (fitness check features-current). Add a feature here, run `python3 tools/features_sync.py`, and it appears everywhere. Fields: icon names a line icon drawn in the Command Center (no emoji); open.cmd is what to type; open.path is a page on the Command Center; open.port is a local app; doc is the guide; highlight puts it on the website's front page. added is the date the feature first shipped (YYYY-MM-DD): the Command Center marks a feature New for 30 days, and every page lists the latest additions.

features.name: Your progress
features.what: Is SecuRAX making you better off? Your Life OS rhythm, what made the estate stronger this month, and the one next step, on your phone every Sunday.
features.outcome: You see, every week, that your days and your estate are getting better, and you always know the one next step.
features.shows: ./securax progress, and a message on your phone every Sunday

features.name: The one next step
features.what: Lost or unsure? One command reads where you are and tells you the single next thing to do, in plain words — no list, no jargon.
features.outcome: You never have to learn 123 commands to be better off: one command always points to the next thing.
features.shows: the terminal, and the end of every ./securax go

features.name: Venture (is it paying its way?)
features.what: Break-even, payback and unit economics for the business built on the estate, counting your time as a cost: log hours, spend and revenue, set your plan, and get a structured prompt that makes an AI stress-test it.
features.outcome: You know when the time and money you put in come back, and which number to move first.
features.shows: ./securax venture: break-even month, payback month, what must be true

features.name: The estate map
features.what: An interactive picture of the whole AI estate, generated from its own declarations: every component is a node coloured by what it is for, every shared platform service is a hub, and an edge joins a component to each service it is built on. Hover, click for detail, filter or search. One self-contained HTML file, online or off.
features.outcome: You see the whole estate and how it hangs together at a glance, instead of reading a list of 43 things.
features.shows: ./securax map: the interactive estate map in a browser

features.name: The suite (built for one, ready for many)
features.what: Every component is declared with the edition it starts in and the shared platform services it uses, so one person's tool can later serve an organisation of any size. Shows how ready each edition is to sell, what blocks it, and writes an honest datasheet per edition.
features.outcome: You can see which edition could be sold today and the one gap that unlocks the most, instead of guessing.
features.shows: ./securax suite: editions, readiness, the gaps that unlock the most; suite sheet EDITION

features.name: Cyber range
features.what: Practise defending real-looking systems against a live red team, with scoring, judging and MITRE ATT&CK, D3FEND and ATLAS learning paths.
features.outcome: Your team practises a real attack and defence and gets measurably faster at both.
features.shows: the exercise portal's scoreboard and the after-exercise report

features.name: Crisis response kit
features.what: Step into an incident: collect evidence properly, find what is wrong, and draft the reports.
features.outcome: When an organisation is hit, you collect evidence that holds up and report in hours, not days.
features.shows: the case report from ./securax respond report

features.name: Purple-team loop
features.what: Attack your own AI channel, check that the attack was detected, and keep the evidence.
features.outcome: You know which AI attacks your rails stop today, and which they do not.
features.shows: the purple-team report and ./securax progress

features.name: Adversary ledger
features.what: Turn every bounty or red-team finding into a purple probe, a lesson and a drill, and prove it stayed closed.
features.outcome: A bug-bounty finding becomes the last of its kind: the estate gets stronger from every attacker, not just safer on paper.
features.shows: ./securax adversary status and ./securax progress

features.name: Check software before you trust it
features.what: Look inside a third-party package or file, in a sandbox, and see what a new version can do that the old one could not.
features.outcome: You trust third-party software only after seeing what it really does.
features.shows: the inspect verdict (OK, REVIEW, BLOCK)

features.name: Readiness for any regulation
features.what: Where your organisation stands on any regulation SecuRAX maps (RBI NBFC directions 2026, SEBI CSCRF, UK CAF, NIST AI 600-1 and more): only your chapter's or category's requirements, each marked with evidence, owner and date; the vital few gaps; VA, PT, IS audit and CISO-to-Board dates; a board pack and an auditor's sheet, kept on your machine.
features.outcome: A Board-ready answer to "where do we stand on the Directions?", with proof, instead of a consultant's spreadsheet that dates in a week.
features.shows: the board pack (./securax readiness report)

features.name: BFSI control matrix
features.what: Every Indian BFSI cyber obligation as one matrix: what applies to you, what is proven, and what to close next. Works with no file from you.
features.outcome: Your control gaps become a short, ranked to-do list instead of a spreadsheet nobody opens.
features.shows: the cockpit's control matrix

features.name: Regulator incident clock
features.what: Every applicable regulator's reporting deadline for an incident, counting down, with the drafts ready.
features.outcome: No regulator deadline is missed: every clock is counted for you.
features.shows: ./securax incident and a phone alert before each deadline

features.name: Regulatory gap maps
features.what: Requirement-by-requirement maps (RBI, SEBI CSCRF, NIST AI 600-1, post-quantum and more) with the evidence for each, checked on every change.
features.outcome: You see exactly what RBI and SEBI expect that is not yet covered, in your own words.
features.shows: ./securax comply

features.name: Risk register
features.what: Your risks with owners and dates, linked to the controls that treat them, with an overdue lamp.
features.outcome: Your biggest risks are named, owned and dated, and you see them shrink.
features.shows: the cockpit's risk heat map

features.name: Cockpit
features.what: One page: what is at risk, what to do next, and the trends. Lamps light only when something needs you.
features.outcome: One page tells you what needs you today, and nothing more.
features.shows: the cockpit in the Command Center

features.name: Govern (for decision makers)
features.what: Where the organisation stands on governance, people, process and technology; the minimum basic and the highest possible; for each gap the 5W1H and an indicative budget; the team you need; a one-page Board report; and a pack of ready policies, SOPs, registers and an executive deck.
features.outcome: Leaders decide what to fix first, who to hire and what to spend, in an afternoon instead of a consulting engagement.
features.shows: the Govern card in the cockpit, and ./securax govern board

features.name: Vantage (the CISO's operating system)
features.what: A phone-first app for a CISO or security executive: what needs you today, leadership rituals, the review rhythm, top risks, decisions, exceptions, tools and their value, stakeholders, team, KPIs and KRIs, playbooks and visible progress. Built from the same kit as the Life OS; a new app for any role is one file.
features.outcome: A security leader's week runs on rhythm instead of memory: nothing late is missed, risks get owners and dates, and progress is there to show the Board.
features.shows: Vantage at /vantage/ on your phone: Today, Risks, Rhythm, OKRs, Progress

features.name: Names, not ports, and links that never break
features.what: Every part of the estate at a name over HTTPS (hub, chat, docs, flows ...), asked once with a one-click move of the Life OS data; the site and docs on GitHub Pages until your own domain is proven live, then on it with one command; every build fails on a broken link.
features.outcome: You open https://hub.securax.localhost instead of remembering port numbers, and no page you or a visitor opens ends in a 404.
features.shows: ./securax names and ./securax site; the Command Center at its name; a red CI check if a link breaks

features.name: Apps for Android and iOS
features.what: Turn any app built from the kit, or the Life OS, into an Android and iOS project in one command: a Capacitor project that works offline from the app's own files, a Trusted Web Activity manifest for the quick Android path, and a store-readiness check.
features.outcome: An app you built for yourself can be in a store without rewriting it, and you know in advance what a reviewer will ask for.
features.shows: ./securax os mobile vantage writes the project; mobile-check names what is missing

features.name: AI security gateway
features.what: Every AI call is checked: personal data masked, prompt injection blocked, data kept in India when it must be, and every call logged.
features.outcome: You use AI freely without leaking data or running up a bill.
features.shows: the gateway's audit and ./securax ai budget

features.name: Private chat
features.what: A ChatGPT-style assistant that runs through the gateway, with a private local model when the data must not leave.
features.outcome: You get a capable assistant you own, with your private data kept private.
features.shows: Chat in the Command Center

features.name: Accurate answers without prompt engineering
features.what: Every question reaches the AI with today's date and the rules a careful expert would write: never make things up, say "I don't know", flag what may have changed, show the working. A weak model says so, and a weekly check catches an AI that starts to guess.
features.outcome: You can act on what the AI says, because it does not make things up.
features.shows: ./securax ai honesty, weekly on your phone

features.name: Build with open models
features.what: Write and fix code with strong open models through the gateway, so your ability to change the estate need not rest on a single AI subscription. Turn it on by adding its CI key; ./securax ai share shows whether it is carrying real work yet.
features.outcome: You change your own tools without hiring anyone or waiting.
features.shows: the autobuild PR and its green checks

features.name: Ship without Claude Code
features.what: The pull-request loop, run by SecuRAX itself: open the PR from the repository's template, watch CI, and when it goes red, gather the failing logs into a brief and let autobuild fix it, one push a round. When everything is green and mergeable, merge and reset the branch. A routine runs it unattended on the always-on machine.
features.outcome: You build SecuRAX with SecuRAX alone: a red pull request gets fixed and merged without you pasting logs into a chat.
features.shows: ./securax ship check and ship watch; your phone when a PR is merged or needs you

features.name: Go back to a working version
features.what: Something broke? One command takes you back to the last version that worked; your edits and data are kept.
features.outcome: A bad update never costs you a day: you go back in one command.
features.shows: ./securax rollback --list

features.name: Encrypted backups
features.what: Backups that are encrypted, copied off the laptop, and proved to restore every quarter.
features.outcome: You never lose your work, whatever happens to the machine.
features.shows: ./securax progress (backups proven) and the quarterly drill

features.name: Storage that runs itself
features.what: Every source of growth has a limit; clean-ups run every six hours, and your phone hears only when space is still short.
features.outcome: Your disk never fills up by surprise.
features.shows: ./securax storage and a warning days ahead

features.name: What broke, and why
features.what: Names the service that stopped and the reason, in plain words, with the fix.
features.outcome: When something goes wrong you get the reason in plain words, not a log.
features.shows: ./securax why

features.name: Crown jewels and risk
features.what: What SecuRAX cannot lose, how exposed each one is today, and the one thing to do next, worst first. It re-scores itself every run.
features.outcome: You know what to protect first, and the one thing to do next.
features.shows: ./securax jewels

features.name: Set it once, then forget it
features.what: Instead of telling you what to do, SecuRAX changes the setting once so the good path is the default and the harmful one takes effort: phone grey and quiet at night, autopay on every bill, pay-yourself-first on salary day, the costliest debt attacked first, a keystone habit anchored and alarmed. Each struggle becomes one obvious change with its one-time steps.
features.outcome: The right thing happens without willpower, because your phone and accounts are set up to make it the default — nothing to remember.
features.shows: ./securax environment, and (next) a one-tap Life OS screen

features.name: Crisis and continuity plan
features.what: Every crisis written down before it happens: how long it may stop you, how much it may lose, the steps, and safe drills that prove it.
features.outcome: A crisis finds you with a plan you have already practised.
features.shows: the tabletop's after-action report and ./securax progress

features.name: Ransomware-proof backups and recovery drills
features.what: Every backup first checks that your data is still readable. If ransomware got there first, the copy is quarantined, nothing clean is deleted and you are alerted. `restore latest` picks the newest clean copy, a restore twin proves it opens, and tabletop exercises test the plan.
features.outcome: Ransomware costs you an evening, not your data.
features.shows: ./securax progress (clean copies, drills passed)

features.name: Guiding Map
features.what: Your daily cockpit for life and work: goals, check-ins and plans. Works offline, no AI needed.
features.outcome: Your days line up with what matters to you, and you can see it happening.
features.shows: the Life OS: wheel, goals, streaks, weekly review

features.name: Life OS Inbox
features.what: Capture one line; then each note becomes an action with a next step and a date, or stays a note. Reviews turn findings into actions; Google Keep notes come in too.
features.outcome: Nothing you capture is lost; each item becomes a decision or a task.
features.shows: the Life OS Inbox reaching zero

features.name: Life papers, read for you
features.what: Your life workbooks and private documents (policies, statements, ID scans) are read on your own machine: every open issue becomes a dated Life OS action, the vital fifth first, with calendar alarms; a missing nominee, a lapsing policy or a password left in a sheet is found for you.
features.outcome: No more updating spreadsheets by hand to know what is still open: the few things that matter come to you, with a date and an alarm.
features.shows: the Life OS Inbox: The vital few

features.name: Your AI history
features.what: Years of chats from Claude, ChatGPT, DeepSeek or Gemini as one private library you can search.
features.outcome: Everything you learned with other AIs becomes yours to search and reuse.
features.shows: your knowledge folder in Chat

features.name: Password manager
features.what: Your own password vault (Vaultwarden) for the Bitwarden apps on laptop and phone, encrypted on your device before it is stored.
features.outcome: You stop reusing passwords, and get them on every device.
features.shows: the Bitwarden apps

features.name: Sign in to AWS, Google Cloud, Azure
features.what: One command per cloud, nothing to install: open the link on any device, sign in, and start building.
features.outcome: You can grow to a real cloud setup when you are ready, without starting again.
features.shows: ./securax stages

features.name: SecuRAX on every device
features.what: Your own address on any phone, tablet or computer: sign in with Google and everything is there, synced, with the laptop off. One command sets it up.
features.outcome: Your estate works from your phone anywhere, like any app.
features.shows: your own addresses (hub, chat)

features.name: Many machines, one SecuRAX
features.what: Run it on the laptop, a VPS, a Mac mini or any cloud at once: every machine holds the same data, and any one of them can stop. Each machine is an extra, never a dependency: with every other one off, this one carries on by itself (doc 90).
features.outcome: Your data is on every machine you own, so none of them is a single point of failure.
features.shows: ./securax nodes

features.name: The estate finds its own weak points
features.what: Every combination of your machines being off is checked: what still works, what slows down, what stops, and the fix for each single point of failure. A new weak point is pushed to your phone.
features.outcome: You know that any one machine can carry the estate, and what to fix if not.
features.shows: ./securax resilience, and a phone message when a new weak point appears

features.name: The autopilot
features.what: The estate learns from its own failures (a postmortem draft and an alert, escalated when one keeps coming back), drills itself every night where it most needs it, and warns days before disk space, backups or the AI allowance run out.
features.outcome: The estate gets stronger from its own failures without you noticing them first.
features.shows: ./securax autopilot and ./securax progress

features.name: Stable and beta versions
features.what: Keep the version you rely on (stable) while a new one is tried (beta), on its own address; switching is safe and never goes back.
features.outcome: You try new versions without risking the one that works.
features.shows: ./securax channel
